title: monitor.json
description: monitor.json is how a monitor runs, and what its fix may do. The monitor's directory, .kiln/monitors/<name>/, holds them as monitor.json. Each key may be left out. The keys recheck, mustAccept and writesTests steer a fix. A monitor with no command and no agent.md names none of them.

$schema.description: $schema names the JSON Schema an editor checks this file against: "../../monitor.schema.json", which kiln init writes to .kiln/. kiln reads nothing from it.

hours.description: hours is how often kiln monitor run runs the monitor, in whole hours from 0 to 65535, such as 1. 0 runs it at every kiln monitor run. Absent, it is 24.

recheck.description: recheck, when false, leaves the monitor's check or gauge out of its fix's gate. Set it false for a problem no fix clears until it is deployed. Absent or true, the gate runs the check or gauge again, and fails while it still finds the problem. A monitor with no command and no agent.md may not name it.

mustAccept.description: mustAccept, when true, keeps each fix that passes on its branch, until the developer runs kiln accept on it. Without it, a fix that passes lands on main. A monitor with no command and no agent.md may not name it.

writesTests.description: writesTests, when true, lets a fix write under each acceptance path's part before {spec}, such as all of uat/. Without it, a fix writes nothing there. kiln then refuses the monitor while acceptance, in kiln.json, names no path with a part before {spec}. A monitor with no command and no agent.md may not name it.

atLeast.description: atLeast is the line of the monitor's gauge script, such as 80. A reading below it crossed the line. A crossed line starts a fix, or asks for the developer in a monitor that only watches. A gauge needs atLeast or atMost, never both. A monitor with no gauge names neither.

atMost.description: atMost is the line of the monitor's gauge script, such as 0. A reading above it crossed the line. A crossed line starts a fix, or asks for the developer in a monitor that only watches. A gauge needs atLeast or atMost, never both. A monitor with no gauge names neither.
